1#main: The laws of mourning during a festival, Rosh HaShanah, and second days of diaspora. And it contains 14 seifim. One who buries his dead before the festival in a manner that mourning applies to him and he observed it — even one hour before the festival — the festival interrupts mourning and nullifies for him the decree of seven; and festival days count toward thirty — behold seven before festival, festival days, and he completes thirty after them; specifically if he observed mourning at that hour, even if he observed only private matters; such as if he heard close tidings on Shabbat that would be erev festival — even though he observes only private matters, festival interrupts; but if he erred (or) intentionally did not observe mourning, or it was close to dark and he could not observe — festival does not nullify mourning; and all the more if he did not know of the death before festival — festival does not nullify; rather he observes private matters during festival and counts seven after festival; in those seven his work is done through others and his slaves and maidservants work in private in his house, for since he was already nullified during festival days from work — even if not due to mourning but festival — ultimately he observed mourning law regarding work; therefore one need not be strict like other mourning; his work through others; all festival days many occupy themselves comforting him — therefore they do not comfort him after festival; festival counts toward thirty, for thirty-day laws — pressing, haircut — apply during festival; and not from festival law alone are they forbidden, but also from mourning law, for from festival law permitted to wear new white pressed garments and take nails with scissors and rejoice in friendship joy; and one coming from overseas, captivity, and the rest the Sages listed — permitted to cut hair and launder; but from mourning law forbidden in all like weekday.
2#main: One who buries his dead during festival on chol haMoed — observes onen laws until buried and after burial observes private matters: {Rama: (nevertheless permitted to be alone with wife (Beit Yosef in name of Raavad and Rosh); see above siman 383 and Orach Chaim siman 548);} festival counts toward thirty completing thirty; even if buried on Sukkot — we do not say Shemini Atzeret cancels; and they occupy themselves comforting during festival: {Rama: All work permitted for him on chol haMoed as matter of loss may do himself; if not matter of loss done through others in their houses and slaves work in private in his house (Beit Yosef in name of Rabbeinu Yerucham);} after festival he begins counting seven; when seven of death complete even if seven mourning days not complete — work through others in their houses and slaves in private; many do not comfort after festival from days comforted during festival; but show him consideration — if buried last three festival days, work through others last three mourning days; in places making two days count seven from last Yom Tov day since from their words it counts and count afterward six days only.
3#main: If he buried his dead seven days before festival and observed seven-day decree — festival nullifies thirty-day decree; even if seventh fell erev festival — part of day like whole counts both ways; permitted to launder, bathe, and cut hair erev festival: {Rama: Close to dark (Tur); on erev Pesach permitted all after noon from time of slaughter onward; better to cut before noon since others forbidden after noon (responsum R' Yehudah Mintz siman 74);} and if eighth fell Shabbat erev festival — permitted launder, bathe, cut erev Shabbat; if did not cut erev Yom Tov or erev Shabbat — permitted after festival since thirty nullified; but on chol haMoed do not cut since could cut before festival; if seventh fell Shabbat erev festival — forbidden cut erev Shabbat, permitted after festival; and likewise chol haMoed since could not cut before festival.
4#main: That festival nullifies thirty-day decree for other dead — but for father and mother forbidden to cut until companions protest; even if festival came after thirty — does not nullify.
5#main: If one of mourning days except seventh fell erev festival — permitted to launder but not wear until night; better refrain laundering until after midnight so evident it is for festival; but bathing forbidden until night; and some permit bathing after mincha close to dark (and so is custom).
6#main: Rosh HaShanah and Yom Kippur are considered like festivals to nullify mourning.
7#main: One hour before Pesach — that hour counts as seven and eight Pesach days — behold fifteen and completes with fifteen others.
8#main: One hour before Shavuot counts as seven; and Shavuot — since if sacrifices not offered on Shavuot have makeup all seven days count as seven — behold fourteen and completes sixteen others; and second day of Shavuot counts toward sixteen.
9#main: One hour before Rosh HaShanah nullifies seven-day decree because of Rosh HaShanah; thirty-day decree nullified by Yom Kippur; cuts erev Yom Kippur; same for one burying dead on third of Tishrei who cuts erev Yom Kippur.
10#main: One hour before Yom Kippur nullifies seven because of Yom Kippur; thirty nullified by festival; cuts erev festival.
11#main: One hour before festival and festival — behold fourteen; Shemini Atzeret seven — behold twenty-one; second day Shemini Atzeret — behold twenty-two and completes eight others.
12#main: One burying dead one hour before festival — that hour and festival count as fourteen; immediately after festival he has law of third week regarding sitting in place and not speaking.
13#main: In places observing second Yom Tov — if relative died on second Yom Tov last day of Pesach or Sukkot or second day Shavuot and buried that day — observes mourning since second Yom Tov is rabbinic and first-day mourning d'oraisa of death and burial pushes aside rabbinic positive command before Torah positive command; but if died second day Rosh HaShanah and buried that day — does not observe mourning, for both days are one long day; in what matter? Seven dead explicit in Torah that kohen becomes impure; those added siman 374 — mourning only rabbinic, therefore no mourning on any Yom Tov; and even those we said observe mourning second Yom Tov — do not tear; world practices not mourning second diaspora Yom Tov for any dead even death and burial day: {Rama: For they hold like those saying no mourning is d'oraisa; custom is widespread; do not change (Rabbenu Tam, R' Yehudah, Rosh).}
14#main: If relative died erev Yom Tov and feared insufficient time to bury by day and gave to gentiles to bring to burial — once taken from city and hidden from relatives' eyes mourning applies; if one hour before festival and observed mourning — seven-day decree nullified even if buried on Yom Tov.
